  title = {CI fails on fixable image vulnerabilities, and the containers run locked down},
  date = {2026-10-22},

  participants = {@lukas2510 asked for the M5 work and delegated it under his account; the AI wrote \#199 and \#200, chose the implementation and merged PRs \#210 and \#212},
  decision = {trivy scans the API and nginx images in every integration run that builds the image and in CD before the push.
It fails on HIGH or CRITICAL findings that have a fix and counts the others; \texttt{.\allowbreak{}trivyignore} takes a finding only with a reason and an expiry, which the scan tool enforces.
A canary scan of a 2023 image must fail.
Dependabot moves pinned images.
Both containers run read-only, without capabilities, with \texttt{no-\allowbreak{}new-\allowbreak{}privileges} and limits on memory and processes.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \texttt{aquasecurity/\allowbreak{}trivy-\allowbreak{}action}: its tags were moved to a credential stealer in March 2026 (\href{https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/security/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23}{GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23}), so trivy is the release binary, pinned by SHA-256.
\item Waiting for the VM load test (\#143): laptop measurements sufficed; the VM run kept 768 MiB (EDN-88: 295 MiB with one worker, 609 MiB with two).
\item Later, in PR \#238, our own nginx image with \texttt{apk upgrade}: a second image to maintain; two unfixed vulnerabilities sit in \texttt{.\allowbreak{}trivyignore} until 2026-11-13.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Counting unfixed findings keeps unpatched Debian CVEs from blocking pull requests.
The canary fails the October 2023 Python image with 93 fixable findings; the API image has none.
The API peaked at 606 to 634 MiB; 768 MiB is 1.2 to 1.3 times that, below NFR-04's 1 GB, and the overall p95 stayed 140 to 170 ms before and 150 to 160 ms after.},
